en: *The Great Golden Peacock King Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle;
the translator’s name is lost, now appended to the Qin records.
The Buddha told Ānanda: "In the past, to the south of the King of Snow Mountains, there was a golden peacock."
O King,
the Buddha dwells therein by means of this Great Peacock King Dhāraṇī Sūtra.
Reciting for self-protection in the morning brings peace during the day;
reciting for self-protection in the evening brings security at night.
Then he spoke this mantra:

Hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ. Li li li li dambali li li li vimali li li. Hīye hīye viśa viśa yugmau kulu irā mili ra ili mili ra citi mili ra ili mili ti-li. He-li citi-li mi-ti-ri dambha-dhu dambha-du-dhu. Kula-kila cchala-ra vi-la-ccha-i-citi-li vi-citi-citi. Ānanda, I now [speak] this for you.
The Heart of the Great Peacock King Mantra-Rāja is now proclaimed.
The mantra is spoken as follows: Icchi.
Jili bili mili.
Mili jimi dantan bing.
Dambhe jvale jvale jvālaya vairocana-mahātejaḥ.
Namo sarvabuddhāṅgulikṣepatomarīciṭihara.
Lohitā mudrā mudrā doṣa-ambā-kūṭi-kunāṭi.
Kukkuṇa jirākusana ci acavata yana bamasa ta sa maciti.
Irimili-girimili-śīra-rā-mi.
Vira-cimūli-dhuta-ma-satumi-ti-hari-mi-sat-pate.
Musaṭe busara busara.
Puṣpāra puṣpāra ina-basita-pakṣa.
Nāgarāja Rāma-vana Miśraka.
Kharāma-kṛte itisa-jale dambike.
Recite "Anadi panadi ananadi" seven times while swiftly invoking the heavens to send down rain and binding the boundary all around. Then,
speak the mantra as follows:
Nārāyaṇa Vānara Aritali Kutali Ilimiṣṭe Kitili Miṣṭe Miṣṭili. The mantra says: "May there be success and auspiciousness, Ānanda! This is the Great Peacock King of Mantras."
Maitreya Bodhisattva, in accordance with what was taught, then spoke this mantra:

Śiri śiri śiri śiri | vada | śuśu | jīvade | hale hale | hāriṇīdanti | śavale śude | śūlapāṇi | śūlapāṇi | bodhi bodhi bodhi bodhi bodhi | satpuṣpa | bodhiphali | caraniye | svāhā. Ānanda, this is the Great Peacock King Mantra.
Brahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, in accordance with what was said,
then spoke this mantra:
*He-le he-le ha-le mi-li ma-ri-ni po-ku-li ki-li ki-li ki-li ki-li-ti brah-ma-ye kau-lan-da-śe bi-tu-ha bu-si bu-su bu-su bu-su bu-su bu-su svā-hā.* Ānanda, this is the Great Peacock King of Mantras.
Śakra, Lord of the Devas, followed what was said and spoke this mantra:

*Dhara | Cāṇḍālī | Mara | Caṇḍālī | Carati-cāṇḍādālī | Mathani | Kāṭani | Gāpani | Hiri | Siri-cūḍi | Siricūḷa | Nāsi | Ha ha ha ha ha ha | Svihi | Jiti | Viciti | Kauluparasi | Ḍuta-ḍuta-si | Pata | Pata-si | Siri-siri | Kapile-kapila | Cili | Hā-hi-hūṃ! May all who are fierce and evil be completely subdued; seize their hands, feet, limbs, and joints so that they cannot move, even as far as the Heaven of the Thirty-three.*
"O you who bring about peace! Śūrapati! Pati! Paśira! Paśira! Paśira! Paśira! Paśira! Paśira! Pati! Svāhā! Ānanda, you have received these names of the former seers."
In the end, there is auspiciousness; one’s aspirations are fulfilled, incantations are perfected, and one constantly practices asceticism while dwelling in mountain forests.
One’s power becomes sovereign, and the capacity for miraculous transformations is swift.
Possessing the five supernormal powers, they travel through the void at will.
I shall now state their names:
they are known as the Great Sage Aṣṭavimokṣa and the Great Sage Vāma.
To the left were the Great Sages Mahādeva, Pāli, Divākara,
Kalyāṇaka, Praticchanna, and Kāśyapa.
The Great Seer Old Kāśyapa, the Great Seer Frowning,
the Great Seer Mountain Branch, the Great Seer Distributor of Pleasure,
the Great Seer named Great, and the Great Seer Foremost.
The Great Seer Mṛgaśiras, the Great Seer Śāla,
the Great Seer Dvaimātura, the Great Seer Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana,
the Great Seer Ātreya, and the Great Seer Parvata.
The Great Sage of Forbearance, the Great Sage Renowned,
the Great Sage Lion, the Great Sage Boat,
the Great Sage Pigeon, and the Great Sage Horse.
They are named the Great Seer Snow, the Great Seer Red-Eyed,
the Great Seer Difficult-to-Conquer, the Great Seer Vidyāpāya, the Great Seer Named Armor,
and the Great Seer Autumn.
The Great Sage Śukra, the Great Sage Vatsa,
the Great Sage Araṇemi, the Great Sage Raivata,
the Great Sage Budha, and the Great Sage Agniveśya.
The great seer Dhūpa-dhārin, the great seer Eka-śṛṅga,
the great seer Ṛṣya-śṛṅga, the great seer Garga,
the great seer Caṇḍakauśika, and the great seer Nāmatīrtha.
The maharṣi Sīmānta, the maharṣi Kapila,
the maharṣi Gautama, the maharṣi Aśva, the maharṣi Vālakhilya,
the maharṣi Nirvṛti, and the maharṣi Gārgya.
Ānanda, these were great seers who appeared in former times;
they composed the four Vedas according to their will, and through their ascetic practices,
they were rigorous and swift, possessing great majestic power.
All that was to be done has been accomplished.
By means of this Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī-sūtra, these [deities] shall likewise protect such-and-such a person,
enabling them to live for a hundred years and witness a hundred autumns.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:

*Hare hare hare, cili mili sūri sūri, hili hili, mili mili, dhāva dhāva, dhaga-paṇi, mathaṇi, thahaṇi, dhahaṇi, pañcaṇi, pañcaṇi, paṭaṇi, ānaṇi, thara caracaraṇi, paṭaṇi, moghaṇi, dambhaṇi, jambhaṇi, svāhā!* To the Four Great Heavenly Kings and all the great kings of the ghost spirits.
Furthermore, by means of the Peacock King Incantation,
may [the name of the person] be protected, so that they may live for a hundred years and see a hundred autumns.
Then he spoke the incantation, saying:
Hekate vi-kate, rāṇi rāṇi, arāṇi, hu-ke hu-ke, phu-ke phu-ke, ha-nai ha-nai ha-nai ha-nai ha-nai ha-nai ha-nai ha-nai ha-nai ha-nai; may it eliminate one's enemies.
Daha daha daha daha daha daha daha daha daha daha. May all those who harbor evil thoughts toward [name] be completely subdued.
Baza bazha bazha bazha bazha bazha bazha bazha bazha. If there be anyone who seeks an opportunity to harm such-and-such a person, may they all be subdued.
Dòu dòu dòu dòu dòu miè mǒu yuàn è hē hē hē hē hē hē hē hē shé dì tú jiè fǎn shé dì.
Jati jati jati jati
jati jati jati
Extinguish their enmity and evil!
Zhou lou, zhou lou, zhou lou!
Jou lou jou lou jou lou jou lou
Cūcū cūcū cūcū
He li he li he li
Hiri hiri hiri
Hiri hiri hiri
Hirimiri miri miṛi.
Mili mili mili
Mili mili mili
Mili mili hou lou.
Hou lou hou lou hou lou.
Hou-lou hou-lou hou-lou
Hou-lou hou-lou hou-lou.

Jihi kṣi kṣi kṣi kṣi.
Cici-maci-de-xian-jixiang-puxian-cheng-yiqie-shi (支翅魔翅得賢吉祥普賢成一切事) —
Cici-maci-de-xian-jixiang-puxian-cheng-yiqie-shi.
Vimalaprabhāśaśivikrama-bhadra (The Virtuous One with the Stainless, Pure, and Wondrous Moon-like Gait)
Ri-ai-dan-toku-du-dan-toku.
Vīṅga-āde-ga-le protect [Name],
causing him to attain a lifespan of one hundred years and to see a hundred autumns.
The Maṇiratna Sūtra:
The Mahāgandhārī Bhikṣu’s Peacock King Dhāraṇī for Deliverance from the Suffering and Calamities of Illness.
The Sūtra of the Great Golden Peacock King Spell for Eliminating Enemies, in one fascicle.
